rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recounting how peoples fare, God reminds the empowered audience of their prior nonexistence and Adam's gifts and fall, warning that bestowed favor can turn into punishment.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر سبحانه ما منحهم به من التمكين , ذكرهم ما كانو عليه قبل هذه المكنة من العدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation and then formation mean preparing the material with a near capacity for its eventual form, assigning each part its measure, as when clay is prepared to grow a tree.
rows.anchor: أي قدرنا خلقكم ثم تصويركم بأن جعلنا فيكم قابلية قريبة من ذلك بتخصيص كل جزء من المادة بمقدار المعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He illustrates gradual preparation by rain-softened soil that can grow a tree, whose fruit-bearing form may or may not develop.
rows.anchor: كما يهيأ التراب بتخمير بإنزال المطر لأن يكون منه شجرة , وقد تكون تلك الشجرة مهيأة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet, in Ibn Masud's report which al-Biqa'i calls authentic, says the embryo is gathered for forty days, then a clot and a morsel for like periods, before an angel breathes the spirit.
rows.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كما في الصحيح عن عبد الله بن مسعود رضى الله عنه : ( ظغن احدكم يجمع خلقه في بطن أمه أربعين يوما

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports in Muslim that after forty-two nights an angel forms the embryo, creates its faculties and body parts, asks whether it is male or female, and writes God's decree.
rows.anchor: وعنه أيضا رضى الله عنه عند مسلم قال : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : ( إذا مر بالنطفة اثنتان وأربعون ليلة بعث الله إليها ملكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the forty-two-night report seems to conflict with the first report and this verse, he reconciles them by taking 'forms it' as preparation during the second forty-day period, near to actual formation.
rows.anchor: فظاهر هذا الحديث مخالف اللفظ الذي قبله وللآية , فيحمل على أن معنى صورها : هيأها في مدة الأربعين الثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He notes disagreement over the embryo's protected status and whether it is permissible to destroy it or cause its expulsion, without detailing the positions here.
rows.anchor: ولذلك اختلفوا في احترامها وهل يباح إفسادها والتسبب في إخراجها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account in Sad describes actual formation, while this verse describes depositing a capacity that brings formation near, reconciling the passages.
rows.anchor: فهذا خلق بالفعل , والذي في هذه السورة بإيداعه القوة المقربة منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse recalls God's gifts to draw people toward concord and rebuke disobedience: He created and enabled them, made the angels prostrate to Adam, and expelled the proud rebel.
rows.anchor: والمراد من الآية التذكير بالنعم استعطافا إلى المؤالفة وتفظيغا بحال المخالفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in 'the angels' encompasses those present in the heavens and earth at that time, whether it marks totality or a generic class.
rows.anchor: أي الموجودينفي ذلك الوقت من أهل السماوات والرض كلهم , بما دلت عليه ( ال ) سواء قلنا : إنها للاستغراق أو الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prostration command came after Adam stood upright as a complete man with a spirit, as the name indicates.
rows.anchor: أي بعد كونه رجلا قائما سويا روح كما هو معروف من التسمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording explicitly identifies Iblis as outside those who prostrated to Adam.
rows.anchor: أنه لم يسجد صرح به فقال : { لم يكن من الساجدين } أي لآدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan describes rear approach as ambush, approach from the right as overreaching, and from the left as deception; 'عن' marks passing beyond and makes his attack surround them across clear, unknown, and ambiguous matters.
rows.anchor: أي ومجاوزا للجهة التي عن { ايمانهم } إليهم { وعن } { شمائلهم } إي مخايلة

rows.speaker: بعض الآثار
rows.claim: Some reports, also mentioned in Waraqa ibn Nawfal's biography, explain the omission of an approach from above by Satan's inability to come from that direction and the risk of confusing him with angels.
rows.anchor: قد ذكر ذلك بعض الآثار كما ذكره في ترجمة ورقة بن نوفل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan expects most people not to be grateful; the author says envy could instead have become aspiration to rise through humility, tears, right action, and counsel.
rows.anchor: ولو أريد بالشقي الخير لاستبدال بالحسد الغبطة فطلب أن يرتقي هو إلى درجاتهم العالية بالبكاء والنم والأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر

rows.speaker: القطاع
rows.claim: Al-Qattaʿ explains مذءوما as disgraced or shamed.
rows.anchor: قال القطاع ذامت الرجل خزيته

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris explains the root in مذءوما as meaning that someone was held in contempt.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن فارس ذامته أي حقرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مدحورا means driven far away and banished from whatever God does not will for him.
rows.anchor: مدحورا } أي مبعدا مطرودا عن كل ما لا أريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God swears that no one among Satan's kind and those who follow him will escape being filled into Hell.
rows.anchor: أي منك ومن قبيلك ومنهم { أجمعين } أي لا يفوتني منكم أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit أنت confirms that the command addresses Adam himself, not a metonymic substitute among those associated with him.
rows.anchor: ولما كان المراد بهذا الأمر هو نفسه لا التجوز به بعض من يلابسه أكد ضميره لتصحيح العطف ورفع التجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ in 'then eat' indicates that eating accompanied settlement in the Garden; al-Baqara's conjunction with waw does not conflict, since a specific sequence is contained within a general one.
rows.anchor: العطف بالفاء الدال على أن المأكول كان مع الإسكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means ample provision and permits eating from everything in the Garden except the forbidden tree; al-Baqara additionally indicates freedom to eat anywhere there.
rows.anchor: من حيث شئتما } بمعنى رغدا أي واسعا فإنه يدل على إباحة الأكل من كل شيء فيها غير المنهي عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prohibiting even approach is stronger than merely forbidding eating: one who comes near a forbidden boundary may fall into the act itself.
rows.anchor: أكد تحريمها بالنهي عن قربانها دون الاكتفاء بالنهي عن غشيانها فقال : { ولا تقربا } اي فضلا عن أن تتناولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eating after approaching the tree would make them wrongdoers, like people walking in darkness; the episode warns that disobeying God can destroy even the highest station.
rows.anchor: أي بالأكل منها الذي هو مقصود النهي فتكونا بذلك فاعلين فعل من يمشي في الظلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وسوس describes a hidden insinuation involving embellishment, repetition, and desire.
rows.anchor: فوسوس } أي القى في خفاء وتزيين وتكرير واشتهاء { لهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive wording means something was hidden and covered from the pair, with the concealment imposing no effort on them.
rows.anchor: أي ستر وغطى بان جعل كانه وراءهما لا يلتفتان إايه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their سوءات are the body parts whose exposure would distress them; their exposure is tied to expulsion from the Garden.
rows.anchor: ليبدي لهما ما ووري عنهما من سوءاتهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He links revealing the shameful parts to being expelled from the Garden and invokes the later account of Satan stripping their clothing.
rows.anchor: ينزع عنهما لباسهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shameful parts are those whose exposure would distress the pair; revealing them is a cause of leaving the Garden.
rows.anchor: أي المواضع التي يسوءهما انكشافها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By calling God 'your Lord,' Satan recalls His beneficence to the pair as a flattering device to draw them toward his desired outcome.
rows.anchor: وذكرهما بوصف الإحسان تذكيرا بإكرامه لهما تجزئة لهما على نا يريد منهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Combining the demonstrative with the noun intensifies the precise identification of this tree.
rows.anchor: جمع بين الإشارة والاسم زيادة في الاعتناء بالتنصيص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan's claim was that the prohibition kept them from becoming angels, whom the author characterizes as free of appetite and able to fly and change form.
rows.anchor: أي في عدم الشهة والقدرة على الطيران والتشكيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan also claimed the tree would make them immortal, so they would never die or leave the Garden.
rows.anchor: أي الذين لا يموتون ولا يخرجون من الجنة أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indecency they excused could mean idolatry or uncovering the private parts during circumambulation.
rows.anchor: أي أمرا بالغا في القبح كالشرك وكشف العورة في الطواف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cited their fathers' practice, but the author says this rationale is manifestly unsound; their real fabrication was to claim God had commanded the indecency.
rows.anchor: وجدنا عليها } أي فاحشة { آباءنا } ولما كانت هذه العلة ظاهرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He argues that they would not have followed their ancestors had they seen them acting foolishly to acquire wealth, exposing the ancestral excuse as false.
rows.anchor: لأن من المعلوم أنهم لو وجدوهم على سفه في تحصيل المال ما تابعوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not command any indecency; claiming that He did is a grave, baseless attribution that brings a severe warning against ignorance and conjecture about God.
rows.anchor: أي الذي له الكمال كله { لا يأمر بالفحشاء } أي بشيء من هذا الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qist is God's command to perform good deeds through the obligations He has imposed, countering their claim with sound reason supported by decisive transmission.
rows.anchor: بالقسط } وهو الأمر المحسن إلي بالتكليف بمحاسن الأعمال التي تدعو إليها الهمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worshippers should orient themselves sincerely at every place, time, and circumstance suitable for prostration, without restricting prayer to a particular mosque or time.
rows.anchor: عند كل مسجد } أي مكان ووقت وحال يصلح السجود فيه , ولا يتقيدزن أحد بمكان ولا زمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Call upon God in worship, devoting religion wholly to Him and associating nothing with Him.
rows.anchor: وادعوه } عند ذلك كله دعاء عبادة { مخلصين له الدين } أي لا تشركوا به شيءا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As God began creation, He will resurrect people; they return divided into guided people, whose hearts He made receptive to guidance, and those upon whom misguidance is fixed.
rows.anchor: أي في النشأة الأولى فأنتم تبتدئون نعيدكم بعد الموت فأنتم

words: فَرِيقًا هَدَىٰ وَفَرِيقًا حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلضَّلَٰلَةُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage uses two instances of ellipsis by reciprocal implication: beginning implies the omitted act of recreating, return implies being begun, guidance implies misguidance, and fixed misguidance implies established guidance for the other group.
rows.anchor: وقد تبين أن ههنا احتباكين : أثبت في أولهما بدا دليلا على حذف يعيد وذكر تعودون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated resurrection reminder addresses deniers by making them familiar with it and weakening their resistance, leading to the reminder that they will be brought out of the earth.
rows.anchor: ولما كرر سبحانه ذكر البعث كما تدعو إليه الحكمة في تقرير ما ينكره المخاطب تأنيسا له به وكسرا لشوكته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an says 'the chiefs' and identifies them as unbelievers, highlighting that their pride led them to disbelief and to try to make their followers reject Shuayb.
rows.anchor: أظهر الوصف بالشرف إشارة إلى أنه الذي حملهم على نتيجة الاستكبار وهي الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chiefs fill eyes with their appearance and hearts with awe; the phrase 'of his people' shows that divine favor may reach a distant enemy and be withheld from close kin.
rows.anchor: الذين } يملؤون العيون مراى والقلوب مهابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They tell followers that following Shuayb would mean losing ancestral religion and the gains of cheating in measures and weights and blocking roads.
rows.anchor: أي لأنكم استبدلتم بدين الآباء غيره وحرمتم فوائد البخس والتطفيف وقط السبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rajfa is a tremendous shaking of hearts or dwellings; the author allows that it caused the cry or resulted from it.
rows.anchor: أي الزلزلة العظيمة في القلوب أو الديار التي كانت سببا للصيحة أو مسببة عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They remained collapsed on their knees or fixed motionless in their dwellings; the singular 'their abode' has a previously discussed rhetorical secret.
rows.anchor: أي باركين على الركب أو لازمين أمكنتهم لا حراك بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He compares the punishment with reports of angels at Hunayn, unbelievers hearing a pebble-like sound within themselves, and an enemy feeling terror a month's journey in front and behind; for Muhammad, the prophet of mercy, this sign brought salvation rather than destruction.
rows.anchor: مثل وقع الحصاة في الطست , ودون ما كان يجد مخالفة من الرعب من مسيرة شهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They seemed never to have lived or stayed there; their former abode and life of leisure, celebration, and self-sufficiency had vanished.
rows.anchor: أي ينزلوا ويقيموا , وبطل مقامهم لاهين بالأفراح والغناء والاستغناء من المغاني وهي المنازل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating that those who rejected Shuayb were the losers underscores their especially shameful rejection, which caused their loss of bodies and souls, while his followers suffered none.
rows.anchor: ولما كان تكذيب الصادقين لا سيما الرسل في غاية الشناعة , كرره إشارة إلى ذلك وإعلاما بأنه سبب لهم أعظم من هلاك الشباح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the punishment, Shuayb turned away and went elsewhere to worship God, as earlier prophets had done when their lands became places of divine anger.
rows.anchor: سبب ذلك أن هاجر عنها كما كانت عادة من قبله من الأنبياء عليهم السلام

words: لَقَدْ أَبْلَغْتُكُمْ رِسَٰلَٰتِ رَبِّى وَنَصَحْتُ لَكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuayb says he conveyed God's messages and sincerely advised his people, perhaps using the plural because he brought many signs and proofs.
rows.anchor: ولعله جمع لأجل كثرة ما أتهاهم به من المعجزات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuayb grieved for his kin because they missed faith, not because their unbelief deserved pity; their closeness explains his sorrow.
rows.anchor: فعرف أنه أسف عليهم من أجل قربهم وفوات الإيمان لهم غير آسف عليهم من أجل كفرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated sequence of five village-prophet stories differs from Abraham's story: those prophets saw their rejecters destroyed, while Abraham left his people before their punishment; the next segment develops this contrast.
rows.anchor: لانتظامهم في أنهم أقرت أعينهم بأن رأوا مصارع من خالفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The five village prophets witnessed the destruction of those who rejected them, but Abraham left before his people's punishment, as he said he was going to his Lord, who would guide him.
rows.anchor: إني ذاهب إلى ربي سيهدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's departure before punishment parallels Muhammad's protection: God would not punish people while the Prophet was among them, a special honor for the prophet of mercy.
rows.anchor: وما كان الله ليعذبهم وأنت فيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion transitions from particular prophetic narratives to the general warning about destroyed towns, quoted as 'How many a town We destroyed.'
rows.anchor: وكم من قرية أهلكناها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He adds the Torah's warnings for Israel's disobedience and injustice to a prior warning in al-Ma'ida about God's curse and wrath.
rows.anchor: ذكر سيء مما هددوا به التوارة على العصيان والبغي والعدوان غير ما تقدم في المائدة

rows.speaker: السفر الخامس
rows.claim: The fifth book of the Torah warns that failure to keep its commandments and revere God brings painful afflictions upon Israel and its descendants.
rows.anchor: وإن لم تحفظ وتعمل بجميع الوصايا والسنن التي كتبت في هذا الكتاب وتتق الله ربك

rows.speaker: السفر الخامس
rows.claim: The Torah warns that Israel's numerous descendants will dwindle, be driven from their land, live in terror among other peoples, and return toward Egypt to be sold as slaves.
rows.anchor: ويبقى من نسلك عدد قليل من بعد كثرتهم التي كانت قد صارت مثل نجوم السماء

rows.speaker: موسى
rows.claim: Moses recalls God's plagues and signs against Egypt and Pharaoh, while saying God had not yet given Israel understanding, sight, or hearing.
rows.anchor: قد رأيتم ما صنع الله بأرض مصر بفرعون وجميع عبيده وكل شعبه والبلايا العظيمة التي رأت أعينكم

rows.speaker: موسى
rows.claim: God sustained Israel through forty wilderness years: their clothes and sandals did not wear out, they ate no bread, and this was to teach them that He was their God.
rows.anchor: ودبركم في البرية أربعين سنة , لم تبل ثيابكم عليكم ولم تخلق خفافكم أيضا

rows.speaker: موسى
rows.claim: Moses calls Israel to keep the Torah's commandments and complete all its works in obedience to God.
rows.anchor: فاحفظوا وصايا هذه التوارة واعلموا بها وأتموا جميع الأعمال في طاعة الله وأكملوها

rows.speaker: موسى
rows.claim: The covenant warns that a man, woman, clan, or tribe might turn from worship of God to the gods of other peoples.
rows.anchor: ولعل فيكم اليوم رجلا أو امرأة أو قبيلة أو سبطا يميل قبلة عن عبادة الله ربنا ويطلب عبادة آلهة تلك الشعوب
